text:
Nina (Design): dropping a quick follow-up from todays design critique — focused on the autoscale control row. main goals: make "min / max" intent unambiguous, offer a clear affordance for bursts, and decide how connected the SLO slider should be to the numeric inputs. see attached comps.

Ravi (PM): we keep getting questions from customers: is max a hard limit? will the system ever exceed it? we need copy that avoids legalese but is explicit about "burst" behavior.

Tess (FE): implementation constraints: the quota stepper component exists and supports aria, but the pool dropdown currently replaces the inputs with a read-only badge for some pool types. if we plan to let users edit min/max across pools, we'll need to normalize the control so the stepper is always present.

Nina (Design): copy proposal — visible label "Max GPUs"; below it a muted line: "soft cap — bursts possible (learn more)". the "learn more" opens a tooltip with one-line rules. also wanted to add a small "burst enabled" pill when pool allows it.

Maya (A11y): prefer short visible label + offscreen description for screen readers. suggested: keep label "Max GPUs", add an element with id "max-desc" containing: "Preferred maximum during steady traffic. If the pool supports bursts, the system may temporarily exceed this to maintain SLOs." visually hide it but expose it via aria-describedby.

Jon (Backend): backend semantics: min and max are stored as absolute GPU counts. bursting is an orthogonal bool on the pool. when burst=true, autoscaler can exceed max temporarily. toggling burst in UI will update pool config and may trigger immediate reconciliation. we should surface a confirmation when changing burst or switching pools that would alter capacity.

Luis (Research): did 6 quick tests — users expect immediate feedback: dragging the SLO slider made many assume the numbers would snap to suggested min/max. they hesitated when the slider didnt change the inputs. we should either automatically adjust suggested values or clearly show an explicit link.

Nina (Design): two interaction options: (A) auto-suggest: slider drag updates suggested min/max and shows a small "apply suggestions" CTA, or (B) explicit sync: small chain-toggle between slider and inputs to lock/unlock sync. my preference: explicit sync to avoid surprising changes.

Tess (FE): chain-toggle is straightforward. accessibility: implement as a toggle button with aria-pressed and a visible label that reads "Sync SLO and capacity". when pressed, update both places and announce via an aria-live region "SLO and capacity synced".

Maya (A11y): +1 but keep live region polite, not assertive. button must have 4.5:1 contrast. also test keyboard-only flow — focus order should be: slider, sync button, min input, max input. when synced, editing any control updates the others.

Jon (Backend): note: if synced and user edits numbers, we should debounce writes to avoid repeated reconciliation calls. suggest client-side debounce of 700ms and batching into one update call. also make sure feature is feature-flagged for Dedicated customers initially.

Ravi (PM): copy for the pool-switch modal (draft): "Switching to [PoolName] may change recommended capacity because hardware differs. Review suggested min/max or keep your current values." CTAs: "Review suggested values" / "Keep current values". Lena (support) asked for a ticket link in the modal for more info.

Maya (A11y): modal needs a clear heading and first focus on the primary action. use simple verbs on buttons: "Review suggested values" and "Keep current values" are fine. avoid "OK"/"Cancel" text.

Luis (Research): small microcopy idea — inline example under Max: "e.g., steady 4 GPUs; bursts up to 6" — testers reacted well to tiny concrete numbers. keeps it tangible.

Nina (Design): summary of updates I'll push: 1) keep short labels, 2) add muted example line under Max, 3) include chain-toggle to sync SLO <> capacity (aria-pressed + live region), 4) tooltip for burst semantics, 5) pool-switch modal copy with clear CTAs. attaching updated figma after this thread.

Tess (FE): thumbs up. please add the exact strings and icon svg so I can size & color it correctly. i'll queue a small PR for the staging branch.

Jon (Backend): creating backend ticket for modal + feature flag now (TICKET-5123). will link here.

Ravi (PM): quick ask — add a changelog blurb for Dedicated customers and a short note for Support to avoid confusion on rollout.

Maya (A11y): left two tiny nits in the figma comments about aria-live messaging and contrast on the chain icon, otherwise :thumbsup:.

Luis (Research): :eyes: i'll run a 6-person remote test on the sync toggle next week and report back.

Nina (Design): thanks all — will update the figma and drop final PR copy in this thread. if anyone has a hot objection, drop it now, otherwise i'll ship to staging end of week.
